summary.value: The Nankin is one of the oldest true bantams, a naturally tiny chicken with no large version. It most likely came from Southeast Asia and was in England by the 1500s, and it helped create later bantams such as the Sebright. Birds are a warm buff or chestnut with black tails, and males are darker with black flight feathers. Combs are either single or rose, and the legs are slate blue. Roosters weigh about 24 ounces and hens about 22. Hens lay some 80 to 100 small creamy white eggs a year and are famous sitters, long used to hatch pheasant, quail and partridge eggs. Nankins are calm and friendly, stay close together as a flock, and make good pets for responsible children. The single comb can get frostbite, so they are a weaker pick for cold northern winters.
